A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BIT speech-decoding work. Text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–S support reliable comparison; the extra page in v5 results from reflow.

before.justification: v3 reports original attempted- and imagined-speech decoding experiments, benchmark results, ablations, and representation analyses in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v5 retains these original empirical results, including BIT benchmark scores in Tables 1–2 and the appendix experiments.

M1.justification: The transformer encoder, masked pretraining, phoneme fine-tuning, LLM integration, contrastive alignment, and inference procedures are unchanged in Section 3 and the technical appendices.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same human and monkey pretraining datasets, Brain-to-Text ’24 and ’25 benchmarks, and imagined-speech evaluations for T12 and T15.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Tables 1–2, the RNN/BIT encoder comparisons, the text/audio LLM comparisons, and the appendix ablations.

E3.justification: Both retain the same preprocessing, validation and test splits, 1,200- and 1,450-sentence benchmark holdouts, metrics, model configurations, and training budgets.

E4.justification: The decoder/projector ablations, RSA/LDA analyses, decoding-error analyses, scaling curves, and pretraining controls are retained unchanged, including the equal-data SSL versus supervised comparison in Appendix P.

E5.justification: Seed and uncertainty reporting is unchanged. Appendix H retains the 10-model and 29-model ensembles and single-seed nonensemble entries; no uncertainty estimates or statistical tests are added.

E6.justification: Numerical entries and plotted findings are unchanged throughout. For example, both report 10.22% WER for the ’24 end-to-end ensemble and 1.76% for the ’25 cascaded ensemble in Tables 1–2.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and objectives, including the contrastive and cross-entropy formulations in Appendices I–J and the representation-analysis definitions, are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and discussion retain the same claims about cross-species pretraining, benchmark performance, audio-LLM decoding, and cross-task generalization.

C2.justification: Interpretations and limitations are unchanged, including the larger gains from human data, real-time limitations from latency and bidirectional attention, and qualifications about pretraining comparisons in Appendix P.

D1.justification: v5 adds a project-code link, github.com/yzhang511/bit, to the abstract. Existing implementation, hyperparameter, hardware, and training details remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish the repository's contents or usability.

R1.justification: The cited works, reference list, and positioning relative to earlier speech BCIs, neural foundation models, and multimodal LLMs are unchanged.

P1.justification: v5 changes Jingyuan Li's listed affiliation from Amazon to the University of Washington and appends the project-code line. The scientific prose and section order otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The added abstract line reflows main-text paragraphs and shifts Tables 1–2 vertically. The broader-impact paragraph spills onto a mostly blank page 10; figures, table designs, and captions remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The explicit project-code pointer modestly improves reproducibility documentation by giving readers a route to the implementation. Scientific content is unchanged, repository completeness cannot be assessed from the PDFs, and the resulting mostly blank page slightly reduces layout efficiency.
